pr_body:
The `System.Reflection.DispatchProxy` type used to be incompatible with unloadability, because the `AssemblyBuilder` with the generated proxy types is created with `AssemblyBuilderAccess.Run` and because all proxy types were associated with a single one.

This PR creates a separate `AssemblyBuilder`, one for each `AssemblyLoadContext` of the base type's assembly, and passes `AssemblyBuilderAccess.RunAndCollect` to it (_edit:_ only if the associated ALC is unloadable). It also cleans-up some code.

Besides allowing unneeded proxy types to be granularly unloaded, it also added support for creating proxies for the same type in different ALC. I added tests for both cases.

Fixes #60468
Fixes #62050
pr_comments: The two tests I added fail on Browser because `Assembly.Location` returns an empty string. Any idea how to selectively disable them?

I would recomend to early out from the tests if the Location is empty string. It will make the test pass in all situations when the assembly is not physically available on the disk (e.g. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/43079).
Thanks for the feedback @jkotas, that was my first guess, thought there might be a more elegant way. I updated the tests.
Hello @d066hie, would you like to explain in more detail what to change in this PR?
Azure Pipelines successfully started running 1 pipeline(s).

Outerloop test failures are unrelated and reported as needed (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/62305,  https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/60753#issuecomment-985084324, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/58616#issuecomment-985081412, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/56165#issuecomment-985088076). 

Thank you for your review @jkotas @vitek-karas if you have no more comments/concerns the PR is ready for merge.

issue_context.title: `DispatchProxy` cannot work with types from collectible assemblies.
comments:
This is discussed in detail here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/60468#issuecomment-975968918

I didn't notice the case where it simply doesn't work at all though.

review_comments:
Thank you @teo-tsirpanis overall the fix LGTM

@vitek-karas [mentioned](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/60468#issuecomment-975968918) that we might want to discuss `if it should always use the ALC of the base type, or if it should react to the current contextual reflection setting. Right now I think it should probably react to contextual reflection, but it will probably need more thought.` I am not familiar with contextual reflection so I have no opinion, i would follow the expert's suggestions here

I spent some more time on this - created https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/62234 to track the `TypeBuilder` problem.

Now I think it's probably better to not react to contextual reflection. If we did use contextual reflection, it would be possible to hit the `TypeBuilder` problem. If we always rely on the base type's ALC that will never happen.
Note that I don't think we will ever really fix the `TypeBuilder` problem, the best we can do without massive rewrite is to actually outright fail creating the type in the "failure" case. Which would mean that using contextual reflection would lead to cases where the proxy creating fails. Not great.

It would also mean that it would be possible to create two proxy types for the exact same combination of base type and interface type (in two different ALCs) - kind of against the current behavior. And there could also be subtle issues if the custom ALC specified via contextual reflection have different assembly resolution behavior.

It still possible to get to weird behavior cases, like loading the same `IFace` type into two different ALCs, and then trying to create proxies using the same `BaseType` but over the two different `IFace` types. But honestly I don't know if this has a solution - either way I can see this scenario to break, so picking one is probably as good as the other.
Thank you for looking into this
